learningObjectives.title: The origins of the Cold War 1941-58
The end of the Cold War 1970-91

questions.q: At which February 1945 conference did Roosevelt, Stalin and Churchill agree that a defeated Germany would be divided into zones of occupation?
options: The Yalta Conference
The Potsdam Conference
The Tehran Conference
The Geneva Conference
questions.explain: At Yalta in February 1945 the 'Big Three' agreed to divide Germany into occupation zones.

questions.q: In which year did President Truman announce the Truman Doctrine, committing the USA to containing the spread of communism?
questions.explain: Truman announced the doctrine of containment in March 1947.

questions.q: What was the main purpose of the Marshall Plan (1947)?
options: To rebuild Western European economies and reduce the appeal of communism
To create a military alliance against the USSR
To divide Germany into four occupation zones
To supply nuclear weapons to Western Europe
questions.explain: Marshall Aid used US economic support to stabilise Western Europe and contain communism.

questions.q: Why did the Western Allies respond to the 1948 Berlin Blockade with an airlift rather than with military force?
options: To supply West Berlin without directly attacking Soviet forces and risking war
Because they had no troops stationed in Germany
Because the United Nations had ordered them to
Because Stalin had personally requested it
questions.explain: The airlift kept West Berlin supplied while avoiding a direct clash that could trigger war.

questions.q: Which military alliance did the USA and Western European states form in 1949?
options: NATO
The Warsaw Pact
Comecon
Cominform
questions.explain: The North Atlantic Treaty Organisation was created in 1949 as a Western defensive alliance.

questions.q: What did George Kennan's 'Long Telegram' (1946) argue?
options: That the USSR was expansionist and the USA should contain the spread of communism
That the USA should launch a nuclear attack on the USSR
That the USSR wanted friendly relations with the West
That the USA should withdraw completely from Europe
questions.explain: Kennan portrayed the USSR as expansionist, encouraging the US policy of containment.

questions.q: In which year was the Berlin Wall built?
questions.explain: The Berlin Wall was constructed in August 1961.

questions.q: Why did the East German government build the Berlin Wall in 1961?
options: To stop East Germans fleeing to the West through Berlin
To protect East Berlin from a Western invasion
To block Marshall Aid from reaching the East
To divide Germany into occupation zones
questions.explain: The Wall was built to halt the mass flight of skilled East Germans to West Berlin.

questions.q: What was the name of the failed 1961 US-backed invasion of Cuba?
options: The Bay of Pigs
Operation Barbarossa
The Cuban Airlift
Operation Rolling Thunder
questions.explain: The Bay of Pigs invasion by US-backed Cuban exiles failed in April 1961.

questions.q: In which month and year did the Cuban Missile Crisis take place?
options: October 1962
August 1961
November 1963
April 1961
questions.explain: The thirteen-day Cuban Missile Crisis occurred in October 1962.

questions.q: As part of the settlement of the Cuban Missile Crisis, what did the USA secretly agree to do?
options: Remove its Jupiter missiles from Turkey
Give Cuba economic aid
Withdraw its forces from West Berlin
Share its nuclear secrets with the USSR
questions.explain: In a secret deal the USA agreed to withdraw its Jupiter missiles from Turkey.

questions.q: Which development was a direct consequence of the Cuban Missile Crisis?
options: The creation of a telephone 'hotline' between Washington and Moscow
The building of the Berlin Wall
The formation of the Warsaw Pact
The launch of the Marshall Plan
questions.explain: The crisis led to a direct hotline in 1963 to improve superpower communication.

questions.q: Who led the reform movement known as the Prague Spring in 1968?
options: Alexander Dubcek
Imre Nagy
Nikita Khrushchev
Leonid Brezhnev
questions.explain: Dubcek led Czechoslovakia's 1968 reforms, aiming for 'socialism with a human face'.

questions.q: What did the Brezhnev Doctrine state?
options: The USSR could intervene in any Warsaw Pact country that threatened communist rule
Warsaw Pact members could leave the alliance whenever they wished
The USSR would never use force in Eastern Europe
Eastern European states could trade freely with the West
questions.explain: The Brezhnev Doctrine justified Soviet intervention to preserve communism, as in Czechoslovakia.

questions.q: Which agreement is the best example of détente between the superpowers in the 1970s?
options: The SALT 1 Treaty (1972)
The Warsaw Pact (1955)
The Truman Doctrine (1947)
The Berlin Blockade (1948)
questions.explain: SALT 1 limited strategic arms and symbolised the easing of tensions known as détente.

questions.q: Why were the Helsinki Accords (1975) significant?
options: The superpowers accepted existing European borders and agreed to respect human rights
They ended the Warsaw Pact
They removed all nuclear weapons from Europe
They reunified Germany
questions.explain: Helsinki confirmed post-war borders and included commitments on human rights.

questions.q: In which year did the Soviet Union invade Afghanistan?
questions.explain: The USSR invaded Afghanistan in December 1979, ending détente.

questions.q: What did Gorbachev's policy of 'glasnost' involve?
options: Greater openness and freedom of speech in the USSR
Rapid rearmament of the Soviet military
The closing of the Soviet borders
A return to Stalinist terror
questions.explain: Glasnost meant 'openness', allowing greater freedom of expression in the USSR.

questions.q: Why did the USA boycott the 1980 Moscow Olympics?
options: In protest at the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan
Because of the Cuban Missile Crisis
To protest at the building of the Berlin Wall
Because the USSR had refused to sign SALT 2
questions.explain: The US-led boycott was a protest against the 1979 Soviet invasion of Afghanistan.

questions.q: Why was the fall of the Berlin Wall in November 1989 significant?
options: It symbolised the collapse of communist control in Eastern Europe and the end of the Cold War divide
It began the Berlin Blockade
It led to the formation of NATO
It triggered the Cuban Missile Crisis
questions.explain: The Wall's fall symbolised the end of communist rule in Eastern Europe and of Cold War division.
